= `+tests/fixtures/metadata_block/+` — committed launcher artefacts

Three kinds of artefact live in this repository, and the difference between
them is load-bearing. Two are *frozen records*; one is *currency-locked*.
Editing the wrong kind destroys evidence rather than updating it.

[cols="1,1,2",options="header"]
|===
|Artefact |Kind |What it proves

|`+minted-2026-09-22_stapeln-launcher.sh+`
|*Frozen.* Never re-mint.
|A real launcher minted by the emitter as it stood BEFORE phase 2, carrying the
retired `+# @a2ml-metadata+` dialect. This is the backwards-compatibility
promise of #40 asserted against an artefact rather than a reconstruction: the
dual-accept reader must still parse what is already on disk across the estate.
Re-minting it is not possible without reverting the emitter, and a re-minted
copy would prove nothing — it would be the new emitter checked against the new
parser, which passes whether or not compatibility survived.

|`+minted-2026-09-23_stapeln-launcher-deed.sh+`
|*Currency-locked.* Re-mint whenever the template or renderer moves.
|What `+mint+` emits TODAY, in the `+# @launcher-deed+` dialect. Pinned
byte-for-byte by `+round_trip::the_committed_deed_fixture_is_what_mint_emits_today+`
and again in CI by `+.github/workflows/launcher-artefacts.yml+`, which mints
from `+../config/stapeln.launcher.fixture.a2ml+` and diffs. Because it is
currency-locked it is also the artefact the scanners read, so a finding against
it is a finding against what the tool produces (#48, #49). The date in the name
records when the DEED dialect landed, not when the bytes were last refreshed.

|`+../config/stapeln.launcher.fixture.a2ml+`
|Input.
|The one config both stapeln artefacts are minted from. A file rather than a
TOML literal in a test so the Rust round-trip tests and the CI mint cannot
drift onto different inputs.
|===

== Why the frozen artefact keeps its defects

The 2026-09-22 launcher carries `+/tmp/stapeln-server.pid+`, an unused
`+APP_PORT+`, a `+sed+` where parameter expansion would do, and a
`+local x="$(…)"+` that masks a return value. All four are fixed in
`+templates/launcher.sh.tera+` (#48, #49) and absent from anything `+mint+`
emits today. They remain here on purpose: this file is a record of what the old
emitter wrote, and a scanner finding against it is a finding about history, not
about the tool. Only the currency-locked artefact is linted in CI.

It also carries a fifth defect, and this one is fixed nowhere: it is missing
four of the standard's required metadata fields — `modes`, `platforms`,
`lifecycle-phases-covered` and `lifecycle-phases-deferred`. The emitter of
2026-09-22 never wrote them and the guard of the day never asked for them, so
this artefact was accepted as complete while being incomplete. That
contradiction is the defect #41 was filed about, and it is asserted rather
than smoothed over: `missing_required()` is pinned to exactly those four names
in both
`metadata_block::tests::the_committed_legacy_fixture_still_parses` and
`round_trip::a_launcher_minted_before_phase_two_still_reads`. What the file
still proves is the compat promise — it parses, and every value it carries
reads back unchanged.

== Re-minting the currency-locked artefact

Never hand-edit it. Regenerate it, so the bytes come from the emitter:

[source,bash]
----
cargo build
./target/debug/launch-scaffolder mint \
  crates/launcher-common/tests/fixtures/config/stapeln.launcher.fixture.a2ml \
  --stdout \
  | sed -E 's|^CONFIG_FILE=.*|CONFIG_FILE=""|' \
  > crates/launcher-common/tests/fixtures/metadata_block/minted-2026-09-23_stapeln-launcher-deed.sh
----

The `+CONFIG_FILE+` normalisation is required because `+mint+` embeds the
CANONICALISED absolute path of the config that produced the script — which is
checkout-location-specific by design, and empty when `+template::render+` is
called with no config path (as the tests do).
